brief_text:
Need to decide how we take £4m out of opex by end of Q2 2027 — do we do it mainly through offshoring support, automation, or closing the Leeds office? Braindump before the exec offsite, apologies for the mess:

- context: 240 heads, £31m revenue, EBITDA minus £1.8m, board wants breakeven by Q3 2027, non-negotiable
- target: £4m annualised opex out, ideally £2.5m of it landed by end of Q2
- support org = 62 people, £2.9m/yr. Offshore quote from TaskUs: ~40% saving on 45 roles = ~£1.1m/yr, but CSAT risk is real
- when a competitor did this their Trustpilot dropped 4.1 to 3.3 in six months (I saw it in their public reviews, not exactly science)
- automation: the deflection pilot in April handled 34% of tickets end to end (our own dashboard, n=6 weeks). Jamie extrapolates that to £800k/yr saving but it assumes vendor pricing holds at renewal — the vendor contract renews in November and they know we're locked in
- Leeds office lease = £600k/yr, break clause March 2027. 70 people based there. Hybrid means maybe we don't need it at all? Nobody has modelled the attrition hit. My guess: we'd lose 10-15% of Leeds staff if we close — pure guess
- constraint: no more than one compulsory redundancy round in the next 12 months — we promised staff after the last one and the CEO is adamant
- constraint: engineering (58 heads) is ring-fenced, board agreed
- assumption: revenue flat at £31m. Sales says +8% but they said that last year and we did minus 2%
- half-formed: could we sell the Leeds sublease rights? or do a 3-day office share with WPP's local outfit? no idea if either is real
- Dana thinks we should just do a 10% across-the-board RIF and be done. I think that's how you kill morale twice — we disagree openly
- worry: doing all three at once = change saturation. The ops director says max two big changes in parallel, based on the 2024 migration mess
- unknown: what does offshoring do to our ISO 27001 posture? the renewal audit is January 2027 Success = EBITDA breakeven by Q3 2027 while keeping the redundancy promise — one compulsory round max. Go ahead.

scope.searched: quantities stated in the brief that carry a unit: money, percentages, counts with a unit word, calendar dates and fiscal periods

items: Revenue upside scenario (+8% sales forecast) — excluded because the brief explicitly discounts it based on prior-year miss and the goal is cost-side only
Dana's across-the-board RIF option — excluded because the brief frames it as ruled out by the redundancy constraint and CEO position, so it does not add decision value
